tests.description: A type suffix on a binder nested in an array pattern decides the arm: the same shape dispatches on element type.
A named type nested in a pattern runs its validator, so a value that fails validation does not match and falls through.
An object pattern nested in an array can carry its own type suffix.
Object containing an array containing a validated binder — the shape a lowered bash command matcher uses.
A nested type suffix binds the value as it arrived; validators decide whether the arm matches, they never rewrite what is bound.
